How Dermaplaning Works

Dermaplaning involves using a sterile, medical-grade blade to gently exfoliate the outermost layer of skin. This layer often harbors buildup from environmental exposure, residual skincare products, and natural oils. By sweeping the blade across the skin’s surface, the treatment removes:

  • Dead skin cells
  • Fine facial hair (peach fuzz)
  • Dull or dry patches
  • Minor surface irregularities

The result is a polished, ultra-smooth canvas that reflects light more evenly, creating a soft and healthy glow.

Who is a Good Candidate for Dermaplaning?

Dermaplaning is well-suited for most healthy adults, particularly those who:

  • Want to brighten dull skin
  • Experience dry or flaky skin
  • Are prone to breakouts from clogged pores
  • Have fine facial hair affecting makeup or skincare
  • Prefer a non-chemical exfoliation method

It is not recommended for those with active acne, open wounds, or certain skin conditions like eczema or rosacea flares.

Frequently Asked Questions About Dermaplaning

Does dermaplaning hurt?

No, it is painless and often described as a light brushing or scraping sensation.

Will my facial hair grow back thicker?

No. Dermaplaning does not change the texture or color of your hair.

How often should I have this done?

Every 4–6 weeks is ideal for maintaining smooth, refreshed skin.

Is there any downtime?

None. You may experience slight redness immediately after, but it typically resolves within an hour.
